primary_sources_read.finding: Held thesis cover verifies Sean Eberhard, Some combinatorial problems in group theory, Oxford DPhil, Hilary 2016. Actual source pages and definitions were read; physical pages equal printed pages plus five after the front matter.
Primary generalization proves the k-sum-free constant 1/(k+1) using multiplicative Følner sequences. It does not establish the arbitrary mixed-sign integer-coefficient equation transfer conjecture.

Candela–Sisask Theorems 1.3 and 1.5 prove prime-modulus convergence for finite-complexity systems of forms, with explicit pairwise linear-independence assumptions. This is not a theorem equating the worst finite-positive-integer subset guarantee δ_F with the finite-field extremal density. The source thesis states a broader conjecture, whose literal scope has an elementary counterexample recorded separately.

Current author primary publication list checked through 2026 records the original sum-free and permutation papers and later group results. No full arbitrary-equation δ_E=d_E(T) resolution was identified in this bounded scan; absence of a publication title is not a certificate of openness.

Author primary Problem 87, physical 41, retains both decreasing p(k) and a constant-factor asymptotic. This is a source-specific current lead, read together with the newer April 2026 paper rather than treating the list alone as current status.

Green–Sawhney, April 2026, Theorem 1.1 proves p(k)=(f({log_2 k})+o(1))k^(-δ)(log k)^(-3/2), with smooth positive periodic f. Remark (1), physical 3, explicitly says nonconstancy of f is presumed but unproved. Corollary 1.2 gives a constant asymptotic only along powers of two. This neither proves nor refutes the source all-k constant conjecture. The paper does not resolve exact monotonicity at every integer k.

Browning, v4 February 2023, proves the set of finite-group commuting probabilities together with zero is closed, resolving Joseph J3. The other two Joseph conjectures are already theorems in the held thesis.

Eberhard–Shumyatsky (2023/2024), Theorem 1.1, gives for d_2(G)≥ε a subgroup H with ε-bounded index and ε-bounded |γ_4(H)|. Taking K=γ_4(H) gives the exact large class-at-most-three section asked about in the thesis, with both index and kernel size bounded in ε. The paper also refutes the stronger bounded-index class-three subgroup statement; that distinction is retained.

Eberhard–Manners–Mrazović obtain the complete-mapping asymptotic for all finite groups satisfying Hall–Paige, using the circle-method approach. This includes even elementary abelian groups beyond the original odd-order case.

Keevash–Lifshitz–Minzer solve the maximum product-free subset problem in A_n for large n, identify all extremizers and prove stability. Thus the source logarithm-removal and extremizer passage is closed, not a new recommendation.

accepted.title: Equation-free subset guarantee and circle extremal density
accepted.text: Let E be an equation a_1x_1+⋯+a_rx_r=0 with integer coefficients, at least one positive and at least one negative. A subset B of an abelian group is E-free if no tuple (x_1,…,x_r)∈B^r satisfies E; repetitions are allowed. Put δ_E=inf_{∅≠A⊂N finite} max_{B⊂A, B E-free}|B|/|A|, where N={1,2,…}. For the circle group T=R/Z with normalized Haar measure μ put d_E(T)=sup{μ(S): S⊂T is measurable and E-free}, where E is interpreted in T. Is δ_E=d_E(T) for every such E?
accepted.subject: Combinatorics & Graph Theory
accepted.scope_review: Definitions of δ_E, the positive-integer ground set and unrestricted repeated-variable solutions are on physical 8 and 24. Physical 29 explicitly imposes both coefficient signs and defines d_E for compact abelian groups. The target quantifies all such fixed equations, not just x_1+⋯+x_k=y_1+⋯+y_l. Translation-invariant equations with diagonal solutions are included and trivially give zero; no distinctness convention is added.
accepted.literature_finding: The source proves special sum-free and k-sum-free cases. The current primary author list, original Følner paper and prime-modulus convergence paper supply partial results with different or narrower quantifiers. No full arbitrary-equation δ_E=d_E(T) resolution was verified in the dated bounded scan.

accepted.title: A constant leading term for limiting invariant-set probabilities
accepted.text: For n≥k≥1 let i(n,k) be the probability that a uniformly random permutation π∈S_n preserves some k-element subset of {1,…,n} setwise. Let p(k)=lim_{n→∞}i(n,k). Equivalently, for independent X_j∼Poisson(1/j), p(k)=P(∃ integers 0≤a_j≤X_j, j=1,…,k, with ∑_{j=1}^k ja_j=k). With δ=1−(1+log log 2)/log 2, where log is natural, is there a constant C>0 such that p(k)∼C k^(−δ)(log k)^(−3/2) as k→∞ through all positive integers?
accepted.subject: Probability & Stochastic Processes
accepted.scope_review: Actual physical 75–79 define invariant sets, cycle-sum representations and the fixed-k n→∞ limit. The order is first n→∞ with k fixed and then k→∞. This asks one constant for all integer k, not just two-sided order estimates or a subsequence.
accepted.literature_finding: Green–Sawhney arXiv:2604.28116 proves the sharper periodic-factor asymptotic. Its physical 3 Remark (1) expressly leaves nonconstancy of that factor unproved, so the literal constant assertion is still undecided; Corollary 1.2 resolves powers of two only. This substantial 2026 partial result is disclosed rather than treating the old order estimate as current.

accepted.title: Monotonicity of limiting invariant-set probabilities
accepted.text: For n≥k≥1 let i(n,k) be the probability that a uniformly random permutation π∈S_n preserves some k-element subset of {1,…,n} setwise. Let p(k)=lim_{n→∞}i(n,k). Equivalently, for independent X_j∼Poisson(1/j), p(k)=P(∃ integers 0≤a_j≤X_j, j=1,…,k, with ∑_{j=1}^k ja_j=k). Is p(k+1)≤p(k) for every integer k≥1?
accepted.subject: Probability & Stochastic Processes
accepted.scope_review: Actual physical 79 separately asks monotonic decrease. Standalone spells out the usual nonincreasing predicate for every k, using the same fixed-k limit, rather than requiring i(n,k) to decrease for every finite n. It is a separate explicitly labelled source question from the constant leading-term asymptotic.

accepted.citation: Question 3.1.7, printed p. 74; physical PDF p. 79.

excluded.reason: Both agents verified a counterexample to the literal arbitrary-system conjecture. For x+y=z and x+2y=4z the rational kernel is (-2t,3t,t), so no positive-integer solution exists and δ_F=1. Over every prime p>3, any B of density greater than 2/3 contains a solution by the intersection of B, (-2)^(-1)B and 3^(-1)B. Thus d_F(F_p)≤2/3 for all such primes, refuting the asserted equality. Both rows have mixed signs. The source states no common-positive-solution restriction; a repaired intended conjecture is not substituted. See root-reviews/EBERHARD-SYSTEM-COUNTERCASE.md.
